title: After 10 years, where are FLP's scholars now?
primary_topics: FLP's law scholarship program (LSP) marks 10 years -- CJP's motivation: none of his five children or 10 grandchildren took up law, so he sought successors among the best and brightest

LSP launched in 2016 with the Tan Yan Kee Foundation (TYKFI) -- third- and fourth-year law students vetted by a board of judges headed by the incumbent chief justice; over P43 million donated; grants grew from P200,000 to P250,000 per scholar per year
FLP's other educational initiatives -- professorial chairs (Metrobank Foundation), dissertation writing contest (Ayala Group), and Esmel Fellows MBA (Metro Pacific Investments Corp.)
Results -- 106 scholars from 234 applicants; ADMU and UP with 15 each; multiple bar topnotchers from the first batch onward

The first five years of practice are 'brutally difficult' -- where scholars are now: public service (Court of Tax Appeals, Public Attorney's Office, SC and CA chambers, consular service) and private practice (major law firms, banking)
Closing -- CJP's legal legacy lives on through the scholars carrying the torch of justice and the ideal of liberty and prosperity under the rule of law

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban marks 10 years of the Foundation for Liberty and Prosperity's law scholarship program (LSP). Proud of his family but disappointed that none of his five children or 10 grandchildren pursued law, he sought successors among the best and brightest of the next generation. To bequeath his legacy of liberty and prosperity under the rule of law, FLP launched the LSP in 2016 with the Tan Yan Kee Foundation, where he is a trustee; it supports outstanding third- and fourth-year law students screened by a board of judges headed by the incumbent chief justice. TYKFI has donated over P43 million, with grants growing from P200,000 to P250,000 per scholar per year. FLP also runs professorial chairs with the Metrobank Foundation, a dissertation writing contest with the Ayala Group and the Esmel Fellows MBA with Metro Pacific Investments Corp. The LSP has awarded 106 scholarships from 234 applicants, with Ateneo and UP producing 15 each. The first batch yielded bar topnotchers Sean James Borja (first) and Katrina Monica Gaw (fifth), and the second batch Kenneth Manuel (sixth), now a Court of Tax Appeals court attorney, and Dexter Rojas (ninth), now with the Public Attorney's Office and author of 'Top Notes in Commercial Law.' Others serve in the chambers of Justices Jose Midas P. Marquez and Walter S. Ong, or as vice consul in Hong Kong; still others are with major law firms and banks, including 2024 first placer Kyle Christian Tutor. CJP notes that the first five years of practice are brutally difficult. Like a proud 'lolo,' he sees that law practice is never confined to a single path, and his heart is full knowing his legacy lives on in these young lawyers carrying the torch of justice.
